messages:
alex.h: Quick follow-up from the runtime segment — thanks for the great questions earlier. I promised a short live thread for any roadmap clarifications or open asks about batching/caching and the kernel work. Post brief Qs here and we'll triage.

maria: Thanks! Quick one — are we still targeting 95/99 P50/P95 latency SLOs for hosted, or are we moving to P99-focused SLOs given recent tail regressions?

ben-runtime: Short answer: we’re shifting emphasis toward P99 for public tenants where customers run interactive chat. P50/P95 matter for cost curves, but product SLO discussions last week pushed P99 as the visible SLA. Can follow up with region-specific targets.

maria: Got it — second quick followup: last canary showed batching reduced avg cost but increased 99th by ~18ms for short requests. Any immediate mitigation planned?

ben-runtime: Yep — that’s the batching vs. tail tradeoff we demoed. Mitigations in flight: adaptive micro-batching (short requests get preferential scheduling), shorter max wait timers for low-latency tiers, and a prefix-eligibility check so we don’t hold requests that are likely to finish quickly. Expect experiments in dedicated canaries next week.

tanya: On kernel work — will kernel v4 include the new fused-attn kernels and the popcount quant paths? Curious about how that interacts with our dynamic batching.

ben-runtime: Kernel v4 includes fused-attn + a new path for 4-bit quantized matmul with explicit dequant windows. It’s designed to be batching-aware: kernel will expose micro-batch-friendly entry points so the runtime can call specialized kernels for small vs large micro-batches. Still tuning context-switch overhead.

maria: Any ETA on when v4 will be available for Dedicated customers to opt into?

alex.h: ETA is mid-May for a limited opt-in (early access) in Dedicated, with Hosted rollout phased after telemetry validates tail improvements. Exact date depends on a couple regressions we’re tracking (KV-cache eviction behavior + small-batch path perf).

maria: Speaking of KV-cache — we saw increased miss amplification when eviction was aggressive on the canary. Are we changing the eviction policy or adding a hot-key bypass?

ben-runtime: We’re adding a small hot-key heap + probabilistic TTL bumping for recently-accessed prefixes to reduce amplification. Also experimenting with an LRU extension window sized by client token budget. Plan: tune in canary next Tue and ship guardrails.

ops-bot: Resource: https://redwood.internal/infra/kv-cache-playbook (internal) — includes current eviction parameters and telemetry dashboards.

tanya: Great — one operational ask: can we add a per-route breakdown in Console for batching-induced latency so product teams can decide to enable micro-batching? Right now it’s opaque.

alex.h: Agreed this is high priority for Product/Console. Action: add to next sprint — Console will surface per-route batch wait and per-route P99 before the public rollout. @ben-runtime and @maria can you pair on the telemetry signal?

ben-runtime: I’ll create the telemetry ticket and wire the micro-batch traces.

maria: I’ll take Console wiring and stub UI for the per-route toggle.

alex.h: Awesome. Final note: if anyone still has open items from the Q&A we didn’t get to today, paste them here and we’ll assign. Thanks all — we’ll summarize action items in the retro doc and ping folks. :thumbsup:
